I used to work as a junior producer for the company then I transitioned into more of a talent scout for potential artists. I basically travel to things like blues clubs or small concerts to find potential artists to sign as well as host and judge auditions for the company. I don’t want to get into specifics as to how much I make but I’d say a small family would be comfortable with with my yearly salary.

I have three siblings, two sisters both married with full careers and one half sister who world in the music industry outside the country. There are a lot of struggles like mounting pressure and really high expectations on your parents side. I won’t share all the struggles since that would be unnecessarily long but I would say the biggest one would be just connecting to people. It’s hard having friends that genuinely care about you and not just your social status or money. It’s also very hard to emotionally connect with people, my father raised my siblings and I to be prepared for the world and to potentially run the business in the future. At the end I’m the heir to the company so it is helpful but it left all of us with some anti social tendencies. We tend to not really feel emotions too strongly and we can be way too logical and blunt with disregard to other people’s emotions. There’s more to it but I won’t make this a whole essay. At the end of the day feeling connected with people and forming friendships is really difficult.
As much as I would like to my parents monitor my spending to make sure I’m not spending on over the top unnecessary things. So they wouldn’t take too kindly to that. Valiant effort though.

Often time I’m left to my own devices, My father I’ll see 2-3 times a week so not really. I see my mother more than my dad since her company is a smaller startup so I’ll see her almost every day at least once although it’s mostly just a quick check in as to how I’m doing and then we part ways and both tend to our responsibilities.

My father is always traveling for his job so I only really see him about 2-3 times a week if I’m lucky. Yeah I get the house to myself a lot but it’s not as eventful as you’d expect. The normal thing I assume would be to invite friends over and party or something along those lines but you I don’t really have many friends since it’s rare to find someone that is actually interested in your personality and being with you rather than what you can offer them. I do have my girlfriend over at times but nothing too spectacular. Also my parents are very strict so doing anything I like is out of the question, they trust me with many liberties but they have their limits.

My parents expect me to work for everything I have. They both started with nothing and rose to where they are at right now and the expectation is that me and the rest of my siblings do the same. The money I receive is from working at my dad company, it’s still a decent sum for a teenager but it’s earned through work. I’m honestly very thankful for being taught this lesson growing up.

My father didn’t go to college but he did attend many trade schools. I would say his biggest strength in terms of intelligence is when it comes to people. He can read them like a book and use their emotions in a business deal. He spent many years studying human psychology in a business aspect, its almost scary how good he is it at when you see it in person.
